title: Dynamic assurance allocator for dedicated fleets: composite target metrics and safety throttles
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Dedicated customers require deterministic throughput guarantees while maintaining cost efficiency. Current autoscalers either overshoot capacity during spikes or react too slowly, causing degraded p95 latency and missed throughput SLAs. This ticket specifies a new "Dynamic Assurance Allocator" (DAA) autoscaling policy engine for dedicated fleets that synthesizes multiple target metrics, applies conservative scaling algorithms, and enforces safety throttles and per-tenant/fleet controls.
problem_statement: We need an autoscaling policy that: (1) targets combined service-level objectives (throughput guarantees + latency percentiles), (2) supports predictive warmup for bursty tenants, (3) enforces safety limits to avoid cost shocks and cascading scaling, and (4) integrates with existing headroom/credit accounting for committed capacity.
goals: Define composite target metric that unifies throughput, latency and queue/backlog indicators
Implement a hybrid scaling algorithm combining PID-style proportional controller with burst-credit banking and slew-rate limits
Provide explicit safety fences (max ramp rate, per-tenant cap, rollback triggers) and measurable invariants
Ship telemetry, dashboards, and synthetic canary to validate behavior under production-like bursts
design_summary: DAA computes a normalized target score per tenant/route by fusing: normalized throughput utilization (u = reqs/sec / committed_throughput), latency pressure (L = p95 / latency_target), queue pressure (Q = inflight / concurrency_target), and error fraction (E). The fused target T = weighted_trimmed_mean([u, L, Q, (1+E*5)]) where weights are configurable per-class (gold/platinum/standard). The policy translates T into an intent: requested_capacity = ceil(committed_capacity * max(1, T * safety_multiplier)). A two-layer controller applies: (1) Proportional stepper that issues capacity intents with max_step and cooldown, and (2) Credit-driven instantaneous burst patching that allows short bursts up to banked_credits. Safety modules enforce max_ramp_percent_per_minute, global_fleet_headroom_floor, and rollback_on_regression (if p95 worsens by >30% for 3 consecutive minutes, revert last scale action).
implementation_notes: Key knobs: weights (w_u,w_L,w_Q,w_E), safety_multiplier default 1.1, max_step 20% of current capacity, cooldown 120s, max_ramp_percent_per_minute 50%, burst_credit_decay half-life 15min. The controller will live in the policy-orchestrator service and publish intents to the capacity-manager. We will reuse existing headroom-credit ledger for burst accounting and extend ledger schema with 'banked_burst' field. Kernel selection and shard affinity must be respected: intents include shard hints to avoid hot-moving KV caches.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated workloads (trace-replay) show <=10% additional peak GPU-minutes vs baseline while meeting throughput guarantees for 95% of tenants
p95 latency stays within SLA targets for canary tenants across a family of synthetic bursts (sudden 5x, gradual 2x, oscillatory load)
No single tenant can cause >20% fleet-wide extra capacity within a 10-minute window (safety fence)
Rollout plan documented and feature-flagged: canary -> 10% tenants -> 50% -> 100%
Unit tests for target fusion math, integration tests for credit bank behavior, chaos test that kills an autoscaler instance and verifies failover
detailed_spec: Metric normalization: throughput_util = min(2, observed_throughput / committed_throughput); latency_pressure = min(3, p95_ms / target_p95_ms); queue_pressure = sigmoid(inflight / concurrency_target) mapped to [0.0, 2.0]; error_factor = 1 + (error_rate * 5)
Fusion: compute trimmed mean after dropping highest and lowest metric to avoid single-signal flip. Default weights: w_u=0.5, w_L=0.3, w_Q=0.15, w_E=0.05; weights are per-tier configurable via console

Controller: proportional_step = clamp(round((T - 1) * current_capacity), -max_step, +max_step); final_intent = current_capacity + proportional_step + burst_patch; apply_cooldown between intent submissions

Burst credits: accrue credits when observed utilization < committed (credit_rate proportional to spare_capacity). Credits capped at banked_credit_max (default 10% of committed capacity). Burst_patch consumes credits and can be applied instantaneously but decays over time per half-life

Safety: enforce per-tenant max_cap_multiplier (default 3x committed), per-tenant ramp ceiling (max_ramp_percent_per_minute), global emergency throttle circuit that limits cumulative scale events if control-plane errors exceed threshold

Rollback: any intent that later correlates with >30% degradation in p95 for 3 mins triggers automated rollback to previous stable capacity and opens a pager if rollback does not restore SLA within 5 mins
monitoring_and_dashboards: New dashboard: DAA - per-tenant target_score, requested_capacity, applied_capacity, banked_credits, cooldown_state
Alert: DAA-Ramp-Exceeded when any tenant exceeds max_ramp_percent_per_minute
Alert: DAA-Rollback-Triggered when automated rollback occurs more than 3x per hour
SLO probes: synthetic clients exercising throughput guarantees every 10 minutes; compare observed p95 vs target and publish regression metric
rollout_plan: Phase 0: dry-run in staging with trace-replay and chaos tests (2 weeks)
Phase 1: canary -> 5 selected committed tenants (72h monitoring window)
Phase 2: 10% of committed customers (1 week), kill-switch ready
Phase 3: ramp to 50% then GA when metrics stable for 2 weeks
test_plan: Unit tests for fusion math and weight configs
Integration: end-to-end test with capacity-manager mock that verifies intents and ledger updates
Replay tests: synth trace set A/B/C to validate cost delta and SLA adherence
Failure injection: simulate capacity-manager timeouts and ensure controller falls back to conservative safe-mode
Load soak: 48h soak on staging with mixed-tenancy patterns
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: over-aggressive scaling leads to cost spikes - Mitigation: strict max_ramp_percent_per_minute and preconfigured burst credit caps
Risk: oscillation across replicas - Mitigation: global intent serialization and cooldown window + trimmed-mean fusion to avoid noisy signals
Risk: KV cache thrash when moving shards - Mitigation: include shard-hints and prefer warm-up lanes instead of immediate rebalancing
Risk: control-plane load from frequent intents - Mitigation: batching of intents and local-leader election per-fleet
open_questions: Should the default weights be tier-based only or also tenant-specific based on historical variability?
What is the optimal burst_credit half-life for mixed short/long bursts? (15min chosen as initial, need experiment)
How do we quantify and bill banked credits for committed customers? Legal/finance input required
